pills.pop_html: Timing: A 15-minute training session, then the ride. Several start times through the day; you choose one.
Guided in: English, Russian, Spanish, Hungarian, French, German or Arabic.
Access: ♿ Wheelchair: ✕ riders stand on the vehicle🎟️ Kids: ✓ from 8 and 30 kg; ✕ pregnant women
How it runs: The listing describes it as a private tour with your own guide, and you pick the start time. It opens with a 15-minute training session, so the 90 minutes include the practice.

Route (Pest side): Erzsébet Square, St Stephen's Basilica, Liberty Square, Parliament (5-minute photo stop), the Shoes on the Danube Bank and the riverside with views across to Buda Castle and Fisherman's Bastion. It does not cross to Buda.
Included: Guide, training, all equipment, photos of your tour, rain ponchos when needed and gloves in winter. Tips are not included.
Per hour: €45 for 90 minutes, training included. The 2-hour Buda and Pest rides (#2, #4) work out at €26.80–27.50 an hour, the 1-hour Express (#5) at €35.
What it feels like: Your own guide sets the pace, and the Pest loop is flat: good for nervous first-timers.

The vehicle: MonsteRollers have 9.5-inch-wide wheels and a low platform, top speed 25 km/h, and run on cycle paths and roads. No licence is needed, but bike or scooter experience is recommended.

Options: From a short express tour up to 4-hour routes covering Buda, Pest and Margaret Island; the route menu includes Castle Hill, Citadella, Heroes' Square and City Park. The from-price is for the shortest option.
Group: Small groups are capped at 8 riders (larger groups are split or booked private). A private option is available.
Price: Reduced from €40 for the shortest route. Longer routes cost more: pick the option in the booking calendar.
What it feels like: Up to 25 km/h on cycle paths and roads: closer to riding a bike than a Segway. Runs in all weather.

Route: Elisabeth Bridge, the Liberty Statue, St Gerard statue, Castle Garden Bazaar, Clark Ádám Square, Buda Castle, Sándor Palace, Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church, then Margaret Island's musical fountain, Parliament, Liberty Square, the Basilica and Andrássy Avenue.
Break: A 15–20 minute stop by Matthias Church with time for coffee or cake at Ruszwurm, the city's oldest bakery. Food and drinks are paid separately.

What it feels like: The most ground of any Segway ride here. No backpacks allowed, so pack light.
